item.text:
**8B.7 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin in 2024**

Overall: mixed, slightly positive on near-term macro activity, but not a strong match for a big claimed transformation. The best 2024 outcomes moved modestly in the claimed direction on growth, tourism, investment, and labor-market conditions, but the flagship consumption program had not yet produced clearly durable results, and household debt, fiscal stress, and rollout problems remained severe.

**Accepted claims**
- [Secondary Cities Vital for Thailand’s Economy as World Bank Projects 2.4% Growth for 2024](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/07/03/secondary-cities-vital-for-thailand-s-economy-as-world-bank-projects-2-4-growth-for-2024) - World Bank, 2024-07-03: The World Bank projected 2.4 percent GDP growth in 2024, up from 1.9 percent in 2023, with growth driven by consumption, tourism, and exports. But it also downgraded the forecast because exports and public investment were weaker than expected, so this is only modest confirmation of Srettha’s growth claim. QIDs: `8B.7`, `8B.6`, `8B.4`
- [Monetary Policy Committee’s Decision 3/2024](https://www.bot.or.th/en/news-and-media/news/news-20240612.html) - Bank of Thailand, 2024-06-12: The BOT said the economy continued to expand on domestic demand and tourism, with labor-market and macro-financial stability still intact. It also flagged structural constraints and weak exports, which means the outcome moved in the right direction but only slowly. QIDs: `8B.7`, `8B.6`
- [Thailand sees at least $22 billion investment pledges in 2024](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thailand-sees-at-least-22-billion-investment-pledges-in-2024-3484417) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-06-14: Thailand reported a 31 percent year-on-year rise in first-quarter investment applications and expected at least 800 billion baht in applications for 2024. That is one of the clearest positive outcome indicators for Srettha’s pro-investment agenda. QIDs: `8B.7`, `8B.6`, `8B.4`
- [Press Release on the Economic and Monetary Conditions for June and the Second Quarter of 2024](https://www.bot.or.th/en/news-and-media/news/news-20240731.html) - Bank of Thailand, 2024-07-31: The BOT said the economy expanded in Q2, private investment increased slightly, government spending expanded after the budget act, and the labor market improved. This supports a partial positive reading, although it also notes weaker tourism revenue and goods exports. QIDs: `8B.7`, `8B.6`
- [Thailand's flagship $14 billion handout scheme suffers early snags as millions rush to register](https://www.yahoo.com/news/thailands-flagship-14-billion-handout-072635149.html) - Reuters via Yahoo News, 2024-08-01: The digital-wallet rollout ran into registration snags and delays, and critics said it was fiscally risky. This weakens the claim that the main household-relief promise was translating into timely, observable outcomes. QIDs: `8B.7`, `8B.6`, `8B.5`
- [Analysis: political turmoil threatens prospects of Thailand's floundering economy](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/analysispolitical-turmoil-threatens-prospects-of-thailands-floundering-economy-3573010) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-08-15: Reuters said household debt had reached 90.8 percent of GDP, car production had fallen for 11 straight months, and the handout scheme plus political turmoil were weighing on the economy. This is strong negative evidence that outcomes were still fragile despite the stated agenda. QIDs: `8B.7`, `8B.6`
- [Thai household debt at record high amid sluggish economy, survey shows](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thai-household-debt-at-record-high-amid-sluggish-economy-survey-shows-3608694) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-09-10: Household debt hit a record high amid slow growth, lower incomes, and high living costs. That is a clear negative outcome indicator for broad household welfare in the Srettha period. QIDs: `8B.7`, `8B.6`

**Bottom line**
- Positive: modest growth, stronger investment applications, continued tourism recovery, and some labor-market improvement.
- Negative: high household debt, weak exports and public investment, and a flagship transfer program that had not yet become a stable delivery mechanism.
- Net: the outcome picture is not a strong vindication of Srettha’s stated economic ambitions. It is better read as modest macro improvement under heavy constraints, with substantial delivery and distributional weakness.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a clean, direct causal evaluation showing that Srettha’s specific 2024 policies materially improved incomes, poverty, or productivity within the same year. The available evidence is mostly macro-aggregate and still heavily shaped by inherited weakness and external constraints.
